issues.description: The manuscript contains a direct contradiction regarding the timing of the experimental interventions. In the Introduction, the authors state the interventions will be placed before the collaborative recall phase. However, in the Procedure section, the interventions are described as taking place in the third phase, after the collaborative recall. This fundamentally changes the nature of the study (proactive inoculation vs. retroactive correction) and makes the experimental timeline unclear.
issues.quote: What is important, we decided to place the methods inducing resistance to misinformation before the collaborative recall phase... [vs] After that, in the second phase, the participants will complete the collaborative recognition test... After that, the third phase will take place: it will consist in the procedures to reduce vulnerability to misinformation...

issues.description: There is a critical contradiction regarding the format of the final individual memory test. The Procedure section states the test will consist of 20 open-ended questions, while the Analysis plan states it will use a two-alternative forced-choice format. These two formats yield entirely different types of data and require different analytical approaches.
issues.quote: The test will contain 20 open-ended questions, eight of which will cover all the critical details... [vs] In the present research, the individual memory test will also use the two-alternative forced-choice format.

issues.description: The manuscript contradicts itself regarding the counterbalancing of discussed and non-discussed items. The Design section claims these items will be fully counterbalanced, but the Procedure section explicitly states that all pairs will discuss the exact same set of four critical details. Failing to counterbalance would completely confound the discussed/non-discussed factor with the specific content of those items.
issues.quote: discussed and non-discussed items will be fully counterbalanced. [vs] In order to ensure sufficient discussion, each pair will discuss the same set of four critical details during the collaborative recall phase. For example, all pairs will talk about Eric’s cap color and his company logo.

issues.description: The proposed statistical analysis (a standard two-factor ANOVA on 240 participants) treats all participants as independent observations. However, because participants are tested in pairs and interact during the collaborative recall phase, their data are dyadic and non-independent. Analyzing them as independent individuals violates the assumption of independence and will inflate Type I error rates. The analysis must account for the nested/dyadic structure of the data (e.g., using multilevel modeling or analyzing pair-level aggregates).
issues.quote: The results will be analyzed by means of a two-factor ANOVA, with one within-subjects factor with two levels (discussed vs. non-discussed items) and one between-subjects factor with four levels...

issues.description: The 'Extended warning' intervention involves explicitly telling participants that their partner saw a different version of the movie. This completely undermines the memory conformity paradigm. If participants know the partner saw a different video, the conflict between their own memory and the partner's statement is resolved (both are factually correct). This tests whether participants understand the experimental deception, not whether they can resist social influence or misinformation.
issues.quote: Extended warning, informing that the partner actually saw a different version of the movie and informing why the deception was applied, should make the participants who are aware of discrepancies discard the consistency assumption...

issues.description: The Analysis plan contains a direct contradiction regarding how discussed items will be scored. The authors first state that if a partner provides an answer consistent with what the participant saw, it will not be classified as misleading. In the very next paragraph, they state they will categorize all discussed items as having contained misinformation. This makes the scoring protocol ambiguous and impossible to evaluate.
issues.quote: However, if the partner provided an answer consistent with what the participant had seen... the situation will not be classified as misleading. [vs] In addition, while scoring the individual memory test accuracy on the discussed questions... we will categorize all discussed items as having contained misinformation...

issues.description: The 'Demonstration and motivation' group undergoes a DRM procedure (listening to lists, writing words, receiving feedback) followed by a podcast. The other groups only listen to a 7-minute podcast. This introduces a significant difference in the time delay and cognitive load between the collaborative recall and the final memory test across conditions, which could confound the results due to differing rates of memory decay.
issues.quote: Participants in the DRM group will be given the DRM procedure with feedback... Afterwards, the participants will be motivated to resist illegitimate influences. [vs] Participants in the ‘Extended warning’ group will listen to the podcast...

issues.description: The power analysis is based on a standard repeated-measures ANOVA for 240 independent individuals. Because the data are dyadic and non-independent, the effective sample size is much smaller (120 pairs), and the degrees of freedom for the between-subjects effects will be halved. The current power analysis significantly overestimates the statistical power of the study.
issues.quote: For the general interaction, that is, between the grouping factor with four groups and the within-subjects factor, the required sample sizes for the small, medium, and large effects were 664, 112, and 48 participants, respectively.

issues.description: The 'Demonstration and motivation' intervention includes explicit instructions for participants to rely only on their own memory and not on their partner's information. This creates strong demand characteristics, as participants may change their behavior simply to comply with the experimenter's explicit directive, rather than due to a genuine psychological resistance to memory conformity.
issues.quote: The participants will be strongly encouraged to rely only on their own memory, not on any information stemming from the partner.

issues.description: The authors acknowledge that demonstrating memory fallibility (via the DRM task) could potentially increase suggestibility. However, because the DRM task is bundled with a motivational podcast, there is no way to disentangle the effects of the two components. A DRM-only control group is needed to test for the hypothesized backfire effect.
issues.quote: Of course, demonstrating memory fallibility alone could have different results: it could even increase suggestibility... We hope, however, that as the demonstration is included in a whole process of warning... it will result in them not doing so.

issues.description: The procedure notes that if participants cannot reach an agreement during collaborative recall, both responses will be documented. However, the analysis plan does not specify how these non-agreements will be treated. If participants do not agree, the social influence is fundamentally different than if they concede to the partner. Lumping these together could obscure the true effect.
issues.quote: If the participants are unable to reach an agreement, both responses will be documented.

issues.description: The analysis plan mentions that 'don't know' responses from the partner will not be classified as misleading. However, it fails to specify how these trials will be handled in the final analysis. If a partner says 'don't know', the participant was not exposed to misinformation for that item, meaning it should likely be excluded from the 'discussed/misled' category for that participant.
issues.quote: Of course, the answer ‘don’t know’ will also not be classified as misleading.

issues.description: There are no manipulation checks to verify that participants paid attention to the podcasts, understood the DRM feedback, or experienced the intended changes in metamemory or motivation. Without manipulation checks, it will be difficult to interpret null results (i.e., whether the theory is wrong or the manipulation simply failed).
issues.quote: Immediately after the participants are done with the methods of reducing memory conformity (or the control condition), they will complete the individual memory test...

issues.description: The authors state that any incorrect answer provided by the partner (e.g., guessing a color neither participant saw) will be classified as misleading. While technically misinformation, this is random noise rather than the systematic, confident misinformation generated by the MORI manipulation. Treating random guesses as equivalent to the experimental manipulation may dilute the measured effect.
issues.quote: All the answers provided by the partner during the discussion (green mug, violet mug, yellow mug, blue mug) are misleading the participant and will be classified as misleading.

issues.description: The control group's podcast is described only as 'concerning soft skills related to social attitudes.' This lacks sufficient detail. It is crucial to know the exact length, format, and cognitive load of this podcast to ensure it serves as an adequate active control for the experimental podcasts.
issues.quote: In the control group, participants will listen to a podcast concerning soft skills related to social attitudes.

issues.description: The rationale for restricting the age range to 16-35 is to avoid intergenerational dyads. However, this range is still broad enough to include significant developmental and social differences (e.g., a 16-year-old and a 35-year-old). A better methodological choice would be to simply match dyads by age rather than restricting the entire sample.
issues.quote: The age of the participants will be restricted in order to avoid a situation in which a very young participant would discuss the original material with an elderly one...

issues.description: The manuscript states there are 8 critical details in the movie, but the collaborative recall only includes 4 critical details and 8 control questions. It is implied, but never explicitly stated, that the remaining 4 critical details serve as the 'non-discussed' baseline items for the final memory test. This should be explicitly clarified.
issues.quote: The test will comprise 12 questions, four of which refer to critical details (e.g., What color was Eric’s cap?), with the other eight being control questions.

issues.description: The plan to conduct an exploratory analysis of 'hypothesis awareness' is vague. The manuscript does not specify how the open-ended responses will be coded, what criteria will be used to define 'awareness' (e.g., guessing the MORI manipulation vs. guessing the general purpose), or how this will be integrated into the statistical models.
issues.quote: Their responses will be recorded for exploratory analysis of any relationship between hypothesis awareness and performance.

issues.description: The claim that erroneous testimonies are 'the leading cause' of incorrect court judgments is an overstatement. While eyewitness misidentification is a major factor in wrongful convictions (particularly in DNA exoneration cases), its prevalence as the absolute leading cause across all types of court judgments is debatable and context-dependent.
issues.quote: ...erroneous testimonies continue to be the leading cause of incorrect court judgments (Smith & Cutler, 2013).

issues.description: There is a grammatical error/typo in the text that disrupts readability.
issues.quote: ...teaching about memory is included is present in a way in both Education about memory and Demonstration and motivation.
